search_audit.query: Open 河 — historical form and meaning
search_audit.outcome: Oracle forms combine water with phonetics 丂 or 何; bronze forms have 𣄰. Warring States manuscripts reduce the phonetic to 可, matching seal structure. Water marks the meaning. Early inscriptions use 河 for the Yellow River; later manuscript examples include rivers generally.
Water began as a flowing-water picture. In a side position its compressed, stylized form is 氵; this form is unrelated to 冫.
